output.title: I built termdiff: a Rust-powered side-by-side diff viewer for git that renders huge diffs in 38ms
output.body:
I'm a terminal-first engineer who got tired of squinting at git's default diff output, especially on monorepos. So I built termdiff: a zero-config, static binary that replaces your pager with a side-by-side, word-level highlighted view.

It renders a 10,000-line diff in 38ms on an M1 MacBook Air — an order of magnitude faster than existing tools. Built in Rust with tree-sitter for accurate syntax parsing, and it works out of the box with your existing git aliases and core.pager settings.

The hard part was keeping alignment perfect in the terminal while doing word-level diffing at speed. I leaned on crossterm for reliable rendering across terminal emulators.

It's MIT-licensed, on Homebrew core, and already has 4,200 GitHub stars. I'd love feedback from fellow command-line users on how it works in your dotfiles setup or with your difftool workflows.

Link: {APP_URL}

(Yes, I'm the builder.)
